grades.quote: By switching frequently between the runnable threads, if any one of them needs only a little processing time, it will get that time relatively soon even if the other threads involve long computations.
grades.reason: Explains the response-time half: switching frequently among runnable threads means a thread needing little CPU gets it soon. It also notes the hedge's limits under heavy load. It does not discuss the throughput cost of the switches.

grades.quote: No one set of parameters will optimize all measures of performance for all workloads.
grades.reason: Discusses tuning of scheduler parameters such as time quantum, and says no one parameter set optimizes all performance measures (response time, throughput). This is only loosely related and does not explain why frequent context switches help response time but hurt throughput.

grades.quote: the convoy phenomenon can also greatly increase the context switching rate and hence decrease system throughput
grades.reason: Says a higher context-switching rate decreases throughput, which touches the throughput side of the question. It is in the context of the convoy phenomenon and does not address response time or explain the tradeoff.

grades.quote: High performance may mean high throughput (Section 3.3.1) or fast response time (Section 3.3.2)
grades.reason: Introduces throughput and response time as separate performance goals of a scheduler. It gives no mechanism or explanation of the tradeoff with context switching. The rest is figure captions on thread states.
